reasoning: The procedure's rule 'A shown result closes the work; the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery' governs this case directly. The row's acceptance line ('his own eye is the check') is exactly the shape the document disarms: 'a row's own definition of done that names his eye as the check is describing one of the three cases base rule 12/27 already reserve for him — a taste call, a trade-off no artifact settles, or a change to the definition of correct that is still an open fork — never an ordinary buildable result a command, a test, or a plain read already confirms was delivered.' Here none of the three cases holds: the delivered state states 'No part of the result is a matter of preference — the page shows what the plan holds and nothing else', so it is not a taste call, no trade-off is left unsettled by an artifact, and nothing redefines correctness — the page shows what the plan already declares. The result is confirmed by all three of the means the rule names: a command (`scripts/render-board.sh` regenerates `board.html`), a test (`tests/test_board_matches_the_canon.py` passes against the generated page), and a plain read (the page was opened and renders as described), and the DOD's rendered surface exists as required, since 'Where the DOD names a rendered or published surface — the words page, board.html, link, published, rendered, url — a receipt with no --surface is refused, because a fixture passing is not the surface rendering.' So 'Once the verifier confirms the observable outcome, the pipeline shows the result ... and closes the checkpoint in the same step. It never leaves a row open to wait for the human to look at what was already shown and bless it.' Nothing here is irreversible outside git, so rule 12's own ground does not stop it. That he has not looked is not a bar; if he disagrees later, 'that disagreement is a new fact, not a reopening of the one that shipped.'
